summary: An excerpt from a novel (Book 2, part 123) in which the narrator, Cas Russell, confronts Dawna Polk of the organization Pithica during a tense conversation. Dawna explains that Pithica's 'insights' let them read people's emotions, but they cannot read or control Mr. Sonrio (Rio), whom they call a special case and have been experimenting on to learn how he reacts. Dawna says they want to talk Rio into a mutually beneficial working relationship, and Cas fears that Pithica gaining control of Rio would be disastrous.
one_line: Cas Russell learns from Dawna Polk of Pithica that their mind-reading insights cannot control Rio Sonrio, and fears they will try to recruit him.
key_facts: Dawna says the 'ship's already sailed' is Cas's reply to the claim that Pithica hopes to change Rio's mind.
Cas reasons that Rio had not known who Dawna was until she put the whammy on her, so he would not have recognized her as a threat.
Dawna states that her insights, which help her relate to people, fail her where Mr. Sonrio is concerned.
Dawna describes Mr. Sonrio as a special case.
Dawna says Pithica's research could fill three textbooks.
Dawna says Pithica sees people's emotions, empathizes with them, and now believes it understands Mr. Sonrio better.
Dawna says Mr. Sonrio is not driven by emotion in the same way as others, but he does have needs.
Cas concludes that Pithica cannot control Rio and that Rio is immune to them.
Cas notes that Rio's abilities do not depend on his skills, and fears no one could stop Pithica if they got to Rio.
Dawna says Pithica wants to talk to Mr. Sonrio and believes his goals are similar to their own.
Dawna says Pithica would help Mr. Sonrio be a better man by providing another check on his inclinations.
Dawna asks Cas, as Rio's friend, to want that outcome.
Cas's internal note suggests that becoming a psychopath would prevent vulnerability to telepathy, which she dismisses as a bad plan.
